newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BUDGET PUTS 20PCT TAX ON INTERBANK INTEREST.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BUDGET PUTS 20PCT TAX ON INTERBANK INTEREST.

text.p: Greece's 1997 draft budget says a 20 percent withholding tax will be imposed on interest from interbank loans.
"A withholding tax of 20 percent is imposed on interest from loans between banks," the draft budget said on page 91.
Reports that the socialist government was planning to impose a withholding tax on interbank deals sparked a controversy last week and halted trading for a day.
The government then announced that interest income from interbank deals would be taxed at the corporate income tax rate, which was raised recently to 40 percent for banks from 35 percent.
The government also announced last week that the income tax prepayment by banks would be raised to 60 percent from 50 percent.

It was unclear whether the two sentences on page 91 were a mistake. National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou answered only a few questions at a news conference on the budget and left before he could clarify the interbank tax issue.
The 1997 draft budget was submitted to parliament on Friday. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
